title: Lab: choose a batch size under a latency target
summary: Trade latency for throughput with a simple batch cost model and find the largest batch that meets a service level objective.

blocks.md: A serving call has a fixed cost $t_0$ (launch, weight reads, scheduling) and a per-request cost $t_1$. A batch of $B$ requests takes $t_0 + B\,t_1$. Throughput grows with $B$ because $t_0$ is shared; latency grows too because every request waits for the whole batch.

steps.title: B = 8
steps.md: 8 + 4 = 12 ms for 8 requests: **667 requests/s**, 5.6x the throughput for 41% more latency.

steps.title: B = 32
steps.md: 8 + 16 = 24 ms: **1,333 requests/s**. Returns are flattening: throughput can never exceed 1/t₁ = 2,000 requests/s.

steps.title: The target
steps.md: With a 50 ms latency target the largest batch is ⌊(50 - 8) / 0.5⌋ = **84**.

blocks.title: Try it: batch size against the target

challenge.md: Tighten the target to **20 ms**. What is the largest batch that still meets it?

blocks.title: Batch planner
blocks.md: Complete `best_batch` (the largest B with t₀ + B·t₁ ≤ slo, or 0 if even one request misses) and `throughput` in requests per second. Times are in milliseconds.
blocks.check:
assert best_batch(8, 0.5, 50) == 84
assert best_batch(8, 0.5, 20) == 24
assert best_batch(8, 0.5, 8.2) == 0
assert abs(throughput(32, 8, 0.5) - 1333.333) < 0.01
blocks.hint: `int((slo - t0) // t1)` if `slo >= t0 + t1`, else 0. Throughput is `b / batch_ms(b, t0, t1) * 1000`.

questions.q: With t₀ = 8 ms and t₁ = 0.5 ms, what throughput does B = 32 give (requests per second)?
What is the upper limit on throughput as B grows without bound?
questions.hint: The fixed cost disappears per request.
questions.explanation: B / (t₀ + B t₁) approaches 1/t₁ = 1/0.5 ms = 2,000 requests/s.

questions.q: Requests arrive slowly at night. What does a fixed large batch size do to them?
options: They wait for the batch to fill, so latency rises even though the server is idle
questions.hint: A batch only runs when it is full, unless a timeout fires.
questions.explanation: Serving systems pair a maximum batch size with a maximum wait time (dynamic batching), so quiet periods do not inflate latency.

points: Batch time ≈ t₀ + B t₁: batching shares the fixed cost.
Throughput approaches 1/t₁; latency keeps growing with B.
Pick the largest B that meets the latency target, and cap the wait time.
